prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1055; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports no airbag deployment and vehicle is drivable. Photos of rear damage received and added to file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Letter of representation received from claimant's attorney's office directing all communications through counsel. Claimant's direct contact discontinued. Preliminary liability appears clear based on the statement of the insured and the independent witness account. Liability acceptance under review pending full police findings.

Entry 3: Claimant's attorney submitted medical documentation indicating diagnoses of cervical strain and lumbar strain following the collision. Records reflect initial evaluation at urgent care followed by referral to physical therapy. Treatment plan notes ongoing range-of-motion limitations and muscle spasm. Prognosis listed as favorable with conservative care. Records reviewed and logged.

Entry 4: Counsel requested an advance on anticipated settlement to cover ongoing physical therapy costs. Request declined pending completion of medical review and receipt of itemized billing. Advised counsel that a records review by the company's medical consultant has been scheduled. Counsel acknowledged and indicated the claimant's therapy schedule will continue for several more weeks.

Entry 5: Medical consultant review completed. Findings consistent with soft tissue injury. Treatment appears reasonable for documented symptoms, though duration of therapy to be evaluated further. Reserve adjusted to reflect current medical picture and representation status. Next step: request complete itemized bills and wage documentation from counsel, then reassess settlement evaluation at next file review.
